title: Renewable Energy (Electricity) Amendment (Cheaper Home Batteries) Bill 2022
short_title: Renewable Energy (Electricity) Amendment (Cheaper Home Batteries) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would let homeowners earn certificates for installing home batteries, reducing the upfront cost.
It works by adding home batteries to the list of technologies that can create small-scale technology certificates under the existing renewable energy scheme.
Home batteries would create certificates for 15 years, but only if installed by 2030.
changes: Adds home batteries as an eligible technology for small-scale technology certificates.
Extends the existing scheme for creating and trading certificates to cover home batteries.
Requires a ministerial review of the scheme's operation, with a final report due by 1 January 2029.
summary.affected: Householders and small businesses that install home batteries.

speeches.speaker: Zali Steggall
speeches.brief: The bill would make home battery installations eligible for small-scale technology certificates under the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme, subsidising batteries to increase uptake, reduce power bills and grid volatility, and potentially add $7.4 billion and 35,000 jobs by processing battery materials domestically. The speaker noted over three million solar panels installed nationally, 30% of households with solar projected to reach 50% by 2030, and only 33,000 home batteries installed last year, with a target of 500,000 by 2030.
